domain: A single Akkadian omen-text tablet (a copied excerpt from Šumma izbu, the 'malformed birth' series) and what its entry-format assumes about the difference between a sign and a symptom
topic: A single Akkadian omen-text tablet (a copied excerpt from Šumma izbu, the 'malformed birth' series) and what its entry-format assumes about the difference between a sign and a symptom

source.title: How the Ancient Greeks Interpreted Their Dreams

movement.gist: Introduce the tablet and its entry format; note it looks structurally identical to a medical case-record (observation, then consequence), inviting the reader to assume omen-reading and diagnosis are the same interpretive act wearing different vocabulary.

Work through both readings in parallel: the physician reads a symptom back to a cause inside the same body (this swelling means this disease); the omen-scribe reads a birth-anomaly forward to a verdict about a different body entirely (the kingdom). Both proceed from visible particular to hidden truth via a fixed, memorized correspondence.

Locate the asymmetry, stated plainly and without flagging: the symptom is caused by the disease it signifies (the swelling and the fever share one origin), whereas the omen shares no causal origin with the political outcome it predicts — the ewe's malformed lamb does not cause, nor is caused by, the enemy's defeat. The parallel structure conceals this difference in kind.

Meet the objection: surely the omen scribes did believe in a hidden causal chain (divine will) linking birth and battle, so the two systems are causally parallel after all, just with an invisible middle term. Answer: the thesis is that the tablet's format is built to make necessity and sufficiency swap places — the sign is treated as sufficient to certify the verdict without needing to be shown necessary, which is precisely what a diagnostic symptom cannot do.

Extend rather than close: this is why the series keeps expanding entry by entry instead of consolidating into general laws like a medical nosology would — each anomaly needs its own separately certified verdict, since none of them explain each other. The interpretive practice is still running, uncompiled, because closure was never its aim.

tension_system.content_frame: The object is a small clay tablet, a scribal school copy of a portion of the Šumma izbu series ('If a malformed [animal] is born'), each entry structured as a fixed protasis-apodosis pair: 'If a ewe gives birth to a lion, [then] the king's enemy will be defeated.' The tablet lists a sequence of birth-anomalies — extra limbs, missing eyes, fused twins — each paired with a political or military verdict about the kingdom, never with a statement about the animal's health, cause of malformation, or the mother's condition. Nothing about husbandry, veterinary care, or embryology appears. The arrangement assumes the anomaly is a message already addressed to the state, not evidence to be diagnosed.

family_realization.note: Paragraph 3 breaks the parallel precisely: the omen has 'no such descent,' then paragraphs 4-5 develop consequences.

ending_behavior.note: The ending rejects a balanced verdict, but concludes categorically rather than arguing that concluding now would itself be erroneous.

voice_consistency.note: Origin-layer excavation and concrete texture work well: 'a copied excerpt sits in front of me now'; etymology remains restrained.

distractor_efficiency.note: Questions offer genuine traps: surface parallel, theological concession, causation versus correlation, scope, and structural-purpose confusion.

explanation_quality.note: Explanations usually cite paragraph mechanisms precisely, especially the paragraph 3 causal distinction and paragraph 4 necessity claim.

answers.reasoning: Passage argues shared format masks fundamentally different inference types (causal vs non-causal).
Mirrors passage: first rule traces cause backward, second merely certifies without causal link.
Shows omens can be grouped under shared principle, contradicting claim series can't consolidate.
Ending states temptation to balance survives because tablets 'look as though' they belong together.
Passage says scribe learned correspondence by heart, did not himself devise it.
Directly stated: symptoms sharing cause groupable; no omen explains another omen.
Objection is raised as strongest defense then refuted by showing format never requires the chain.
No disambiguation procedure shows sign alone certifies verdict without necessity check, unlike rival B option.
